name: claude-dashboard
description: Unofficial. A 23-tab dashboard over every Claude Code transcript on the machine — spend, agents, workflows, limits — and a configurable status bar for the numbers you want in front of you.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Reads only Claude Code's own state under the home directory; nothing from the workspace is executed or trusted.

virtualWorkspaces.description: No workspace file is ever read; the workspace path is used only to match Claude sessions of this repository, and in a virtual workspace that match finds nothing.

commands.title: Claude: Export usage as CSV or JSON
Claude: Copy the workflow run id

claudeStatusline.segments.markdownDescription:
One status-bar item per string, left to right. Write literal text, `{placeholders}`, and `[optional groups]` that vanish whole when a placeholder inside them has nothing to say. A segment whose placeholders are all empty hides itself.

Run **Claude Statusline: List status-bar placeholders** to see every name with the value it has right now.

Limits: `{weekly}` `{weeklyBar}` `{plan}` `{drift}` `{dry}` `{dryAt}` `{dryLeft}` `{reset}` `{resetLeft}` `{session5h}` `{session5hLeft}` `{scoped}` `{scoped:Opus}`

Session: `{ctx}` `{ctxTokens}` `{ctxWindow}` `{ctxCache}` `{compact}` `{model}` `{effort}` `{advisor}` `{thinking}` `{outputStyle}` `{branch}` `{version}` `{update}`

Spend: `{cost}` `{burn}` `{today}` `{requests}` `{duration}` `{apiShare}` `{added}` `{removed}`

Work: `{peers}` `{peersBusy}` `{todo}` `{todoActive}` `{jobs}` `{sessions}` `{openTasks}`

Workflow: `{wfName}` `{wfAgents}` `{wfElapsed}` `{wfCost}` `{wfRuns}`

VS Code icons work too: `$(flame)`, `$(rocket)`. A backslash escapes `{`, `}`, `[` and `]`.

claudeStatusline.fetchLimits.markdownDescription:
Ask Anthropic for the account's limits.

When on, the extension reads the OAuth token Claude Code already stores (macOS Keychain, falling back to `~/.claude/.credentials.json`) and sends it in one `Authorization` header to `https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage` — the same endpoint `/usage` reads. The answer is cached in `~/.claude/statusline-usage.json`, shared with `statusline.sh`, at most once a minute per machine. The token is not stored, copied or sent anywhere else.

When off, nothing leaves the machine and the token is never read. Limit fields then come from that cache if something else wrote it, and stay empty otherwise; everything drawn from local transcripts — context, spend, workflows, the dashboard — is unaffected.

claudeStatusline.autoRefresh.markdownDescription:
Redraw the dashboard and the status bar on a timer.

On, both refresh every `claudeStatusline.refreshInterval` seconds. Off, the status bar still updates from the cheap ten-second read, but the expensive pass — the full transcript index, the spend across every project, the limits request — happens only when you ask for it with **Reindex** or **Claude: Refresh now**.

Turn it off on battery, or while a page is open that you want to keep still.

claudeStatusline.monthlyBudget.markdownDescription:
A spend ceiling for the calendar month, in dollars.

Set it above zero and the dashboard draws the month against it and the extension says so once at 80% and once at 100% — once per month each, not on every tick. Zero turns both off.

The figure is an estimate from public per-million-token rates across every transcript on this machine, not a bill.

claudeStatusline.fetchChangelog.markdownDescription:
Fetch the full Claude Code changelog.

**Off by default.** With it off, the Changelog tab reads the copy the client already keeps in `~/.claude/cache/changelog.md` — which covers the version running and a little history, and lags a release by up to a day.

With it on, the extension fetches `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/CHANGELOG.md` — one public file, no credentials, at most once an hour — and shows every release Anthropic has published. The answer is cached in the extension's own storage.

claudeStatusline.checkPluginUpdates.markdownDescription:
Ask each plugin's marketplace whether a newer version exists.

**Off by default, and off means nothing leaves the machine.** With it off the Health tab still lists every installed plugin, its version and what actually ran — it simply cannot tell you which of them is out of date, because that answer only exists on a server.

With it on, the extension fetches the marketplace manifest each plugin was installed from, at most once an hour, and compares versions. No credentials are sent and nothing about your usage is transmitted — only a request for a public manifest.

enumDescriptions: A tab in the editor group you are looking at, among the files open there.
A tab in a new editor group split off to the right — where Claude Code's own button puts it.
The terminal panel at the bottom, beside the other terminals.
A tab that is moved straight out into a window of its own.
claudeStatusline.openLocation.markdownDescription:
Where **Open Claude Code** puts the session — the button in the status bar, the one in the editor's title bar, and the command, all three.

The session is the same everywhere: a terminal running `claude` from the shell's `PATH`. Only the place differs, and it is read at the moment you press the button, so changing it needs no reload.

enumDescriptions: Whatever the client would start on by itself — no --model flag is passed.
Latest Opus, on its ordinary context window.
Latest Opus with the million-token context window — a variant of the same model, not the same thing as the entry above.
Latest Sonnet, on its ordinary context window.
Latest Sonnet with the million-token context window.
Latest Fable, on its ordinary context window.
Latest Fable with the million-token context window.
Latest Haiku.
Whichever the client considers best for the task.
Opus while planning, Sonnet for everything else.
claudeStatusline.model.markdownDescription:
Start the session on this model, as `claude --model <alias>`.

The list is the aliases the client itself accepts; a dated or otherwise exact model id goes in `claudeStatusline.launchArgs` instead, as `--model claude-opus-5-20260101`.

Empty means no flag at all, which leaves the choice to the client — its own settings, the project's `.claude/settings.json`, and whatever `/model` was last set to.

enumDescriptions: Whatever the client would start on by itself — no --effort flag is passed.
Shallowest reasoning, fastest answers.
Moderate reasoning.
Deep reasoning — the default of most models.
Deeper still.
Deepest reasoning, at the cost of tokens and time.
claudeStatusline.effort.markdownDescription:
Start the session at this effort, as `claude --effort <level>`.

Empty means no flag, leaving the level to the client and its settings. A model that does not offer the level asked for quietly runs at the highest one it has.

enumDescriptions: No advisor — the flag is not passed and the client's own setting stands.
Latest Opus as the advisor.
Latest Sonnet as the advisor.
Latest Fable as the advisor.
Latest Haiku as the advisor.
claudeStatusline.advisor.markdownDescription:
Turn on the server-side advisor for the session, as `claude --advisor <model>` — a second model that reads the whole conversation and advises the one doing the work.

The client hides this flag from its own `--help`, but it is a real option and takes an alias or a full model id; an exact id goes in `claudeStatusline.launchArgs` instead.

Empty passes no flag, which leaves whatever `advisorModel` the client already has. The advisor must rank at or above the model it advises, and the client refuses the pair if it does not.

enumDescriptions: No style is asked for — whatever the client's own settings say.
Claude Code's ordinary system prompt for software engineering.
Executes immediately, makes reasonable assumptions instead of pausing for routine decisions, prefers action over planning.
Adds educational "Insights" between the steps of a task.
Learn by doing: insights plus TODO(human) markers for you to fill in.
claudeStatusline.outputStyle.markdownDescription:
Ask for an output style for the session — how Claude answers, not what it can do.

There is no command-line flag for this: `outputStyle` is an ordinary setting, so it travels as `claude --settings '{"outputStyle":"…"}'`, which **merges** with your settings files rather than replacing them — every other key keeps whatever value it already had.

The list is the client's four built-in styles. A style of your own lives in `~/.claude/output-styles`; pass its name through `claudeStatusline.launchArgs` instead.

claudeStatusline.launchArgs.markdownDescription:
Anything else to put on the command line, after the two flags above — `--permission-mode acceptEdits`, `--fallback-model sonnet`, an exact model id.

Written into the shell exactly as typed, so quoting is yours: a value with brackets in it, such as a `[1m]` suffix, has to be quoted or the shell will read it as a pattern.

This one is yours alone — a project cannot set it through `.vscode/settings.json`, because free text going into a shell is not something a repository you opened should be able to choose.

claudeStatusline.renameTabs.markdownDescription:
Name each terminal opened by **Open Claude Code** after the session running in it, following `/rename` and the generated title as they change.

Only terminals this extension opened are renamed, and only while one of them is the active terminal — VS Code's rename acts on the active terminal, so a background one could only be renamed by first switching to it. A terminal opened by the button is active from the start, and any of them is renamed the moment you switch back to it.

Off, they keep the name they were opened with.

claudeStatusline.refreshInterval.description: How often to refresh limits and session stats, in seconds.

claudeStatusline.alignment.description: Which side of the status bar to use. Applied immediately.

claudeStatusline.priority.description: Priority within the chosen side: higher means further left. Applied immediately.
